news.title: OpenAI launches Images 2.6 with GIF creation and image references
news.description: OpenAI is rolling out Images 2.6 in ChatGPT and Codex, with 50% faster generation and the ability to create GIFs. Users can adjust the speed, edit each image, and share them.

news.title: Apple cuts internal AI usage budgets
news.description: Apple has reduced the daily spending limits for AI models used by its employees. Some engineering budgets are dropping from $300 to $200, with further cuts under consideration for certain teams.

news.title: SpaceX commercializes Starfall, its orbital reentry capsule
news.description: SpaceX has launched a commercial page for Starfall, a disk-shaped reentry capsule capable of carrying up to 1,000 kg. It can provide 1 kW of electricity and transmit data via Starlink while in orbit.

news.title: ChatGPT reportedly accounts for about 20% of Google’s search volume
news.description: OpenAI Chief Product Officer Adam Fry says ChatGPT has reached about 20% of Google’s search volume. If accurate, the chatbot would be Google Search’s most serious challenger in decades.

news.title: Meta changes the names of its artificial intelligence models
news.description: Meta has made an important decision about how it names its AI models. Charles Rollet details the change.

news.title: Elon Musk spent $446 million supporting Republicans
news.description: Elon Musk spent $446 million supporting the Republican Party, including $224 million in Texas, which became Democratic. Tesla and SpaceX shares ended lower on Wednesday.

news.title: Cat Wu joins OpenAI after leaving Anthropic
news.description: The former head of Claude Code product will now lead core product management at OpenAI. Her hiring is a major win for OpenAI ahead of Anthropic’s expected IPO.

news.title: The AI boom turns fiber-optic cables into coveted assets
news.description: The artificial intelligence boom is making fiber-optic cables highly sought-after commodities.

news.title: OpenAI plans to acquire code-hosting startup Pierre
news.description: OpenAI has agreed to acquire Pierre Computer, the startup that already hosts Codex’s code repositories. The deal brings OpenAI closer to GitHub’s territory.

news.title: Chris Lehane presents OpenAI’s 2028 policy agenda
news.description: OpenAI’s Chris Lehane presented a 2028 policy program covering workers, education, safety and data centers.

news.title: An open tissue atlas aims to improve AI against cancer
news.description: Scientists at EPFL have created spora, described as the largest open collection of tissue images, to help artificial intelligence better understand cancer.

news.title: Switzerland bets on open and sovereign AI against tech giants
news.description: Facing the dominance of American and Chinese AI giants, Switzerland is betting on open and sovereign AI.

news.title: The Swiss are using AI extensively to interpret their symptoms
news.description: Artificial intelligence is rapidly becoming part of Swiss healthcare habits, according to the CSS study on the subject.

news.title: Varda manufactures drugs in microgravity
news.description: Varda Space Industries uses autonomous orbital factories to process materials in small laboratories before returning a capsule to Earth. The company plans seven missions in 2027 and ten in 2028.

news.title: X.com rebuilds its web app with five engineers and AI agents
news.description: X.com’s new web application was developed by five engineers working with AI coding agents in less than six months. It loads significantly faster than the old version on slow connections and already serves logged-out users.

news.title: Design engineers use prototypes to shape future software
news.description: Design engineers contribute to feature and architecture decisions in code while retaining their role as designers. Their position enables them to create compelling prototypes of future concepts.

news.title: Local opposition to data centers gains ground across the US
news.description: Nearly all local measures put to a vote opposing data centers have passed or are on track to do so, with the exception of North Dakota. This political constraint could keep AI in a state of scarcity longer than expected.

news.title: Voice remains underused as an interface for AI
news.description: Voice is presented as a natural interface, particularly for speaking freely with coding agents and capturing context. The article outlines several ways to use voice to interact with AI.

news.title: Sequoia scales back its expansion and reorganizes its operations
news.description: Sequoia Capital is closing its London office, ending its Arc accelerator and Scouts program, and merging its early-stage and growth teams. The firm has also flattened its partnership structure and eliminated its Monday meeting.

news.title: US AI capacity could reach a ceiling of 81 GW in 2027
news.description: US capacity dedicated to AI is expected to rise from 38 GW today to a ceiling of 81 GW in 2027.

news.title: Teams need to choose bugs to fix more carefully
news.description: It is no longer practical to fix every bug. Teams therefore need to be more selective about the problems they devote their efforts to.

news.title: YouTube is preparing Tamba, an experimental app with social features
news.description: Tamba could serve as a testing ground for social features rather than being a finished product.

news.title: The biggest AI spenders stagnate in the third quarter
news.description: AI adoption continues to grow among other companies, but spending by the top 1% of customers stagnated in the third quarter. Anthropic’s dollar growth also slowed.

news.title: Payments could replace advertising revenue in the agent era
news.description: Agents make advertising-based business models less effective. Agent-driven spending could offset part of the decline in revenue.

news.title: Goldman Sachs limits AI coding tools for its technical teams
news.description: Goldman Sachs has limited the use of AI-based coding tools among its technical teams, excluding most traders and bankers for security reasons.

news.title: Create an on-demand data analyst with Grok Bot
news.description: The tutorial explains how to create a Bot dedicated to analyzing business data, connect it to data sources, and provide the necessary business context. The Bot can then be shared with the team and used from Team Bots or Slack.

news.title: Personal agents threaten the subscription economy
news.description: Agents can cancel subscriptions, negotiate bills, and move money into higher-yielding accounts. They could save customers time and money while disrupting entire industries.

news.title: Anthropic warns of the risk of critical thinking disappearing
news.description: Anthropic’s Addy Osmani believes critical thinking could disappear as agents become constantly available. His article on protecting this ability has surpassed three million views.

news.title: A Chrome extension replaces YouTube’s clickbait thumbnails
news.description: The De-Slopping YouTube Chrome extension replaces thumbnails designed to attract clicks with an image taken from the video, providing a better indication of what viewers will watch.

news.title: Claude Code subagents use 99% fewer resources
news.description: An update reduces Claude Code subagents’ resource consumption by 99%. Anthropic also published a roundup of the product’s major updates in October.

news.title: The blue wave puts tech’s right wing on the defensive
news.description: The 2026 midterm elections dealt a major public setback to a tech industry that had moved closer to Republicans. The infrastructure needed for AI’s future, particularly data centers, is at the heart of the backlash.

news.title: Voters oppose new AI infrastructure in their region
news.description: According to an NBC News exit poll, a majority of voters say AI and data centers played an important role in their vote. They also say they oppose new AI infrastructure in their community.

news.title: A small North Dakota town supports data centers
news.description: A small town in North Dakota is the only place presented as having voted in favor of data centers.

news.title: Neocloud stocks fall after the U.S. elections
news.description: Shares of CoreWeave, Nebius and Iren fell, while the tech sector overall ended the session higher. A slowdown among AI companies could nevertheless reduce the risk of supply exceeding demand.

news.title: California’s billionaire wealth tax is in trouble
news.description: Early results for Proposition 40 show the “no” vote with a clear lead. The final count is not yet known.

news.title: U.S. futures are mixed ahead of the jobs report
news.description: U.S. stock futures were moving in different directions on Thursday. Investors are weighing the post-election rebound ahead of Friday’s jobs report.

news.title: A rare recession indicator has flashed
news.description: The S&P 500’s forward price-to-earnings ratio, an indicator that has historically appeared around recessions, has fallen sharply. In most years when the ratio dropped significantly, the United States was in a recession or bear market.

news.title: The skills that matter most on Wall Street in the AI era
news.description: AI is changing the qualities that help people stand out when starting out on Wall Street. Business Insider’s Rising Stars explain which skills to develop as AI automates an increasing share of the work.

news.title: The blue wave could boost markets through political gridlock
news.description: Democratic victories in Congress could produce political gridlock that has historically benefited markets. They will also affect AI-related stocks, the war in Iran and the deficit.

news.title: Robots are transforming the work of Ukrainian frontline soldiers
news.description: Robots now perform tasks that previously exposed soldiers to danger, such as transporting ammunition or evacuating troops from combat zones. Several Ukrainian military personnel describe an increasingly robotic war.

news.title: Delays threaten Microsoft’s AI data-center partners
news.description: Microsoft cut its annual capital-spending forecast by $5 billion, with its CFO citing delays at third-party cloud providers among other factors. Satellite analysis suggests that two data-center projects could be affected.

news.title: Executives are beginning to regret forcing AI on their employees
news.description: After pushing employees to adopt AI, executives are facing an abundance of bland, low-quality content resulting from their own policies.

news.title: Canva offers support to more than 1,200 laid-off employees
news.description: Canva is offering more than 1,200 departing employees interview preparation, LinkedIn Premium, access to its network, and the opportunity to apply for $10,000 grants to create a startup. Verizon and Chevron have also introduced reskilling programs.

news.title: Good Good’s former marketing director sues the company for defamation
news.description: Jeff Lefkovits, Good Good’s former marketing director, says he was made a scapegoat after the advertising fiasco. He is seeking more than $1 million from the company and its former executive.

news.title: The nanny killed in the Learjet crash held a biomedical engineering degree
news.description: The nanny who died in the Learjet crash had earned a degree in biomedical engineering.

news.title: Grocers oppose the DoorDash–Instacart deal
news.description: Food retailers are challenging the agreement between DoorDash and Instacart.

news.title: Retail’s seasonal jobs are leaving store floors
news.description: Temporary holiday-season jobs are gradually moving away from the sales floor.

news.title: Zohran Mamdani’s pied-à-terre tax clears a legal hurdle
news.description: The pied-à-terre tax backed by New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani scored a major victory in court.

news.title: Barry Diller advises Hollywood to stop chasing Netflix
news.description: Barry Diller believes Hollywood should stop trying to imitate or catch up with Netflix.

news.title: The Learjet crash prompts high-profile figures to reconsider private aviation
news.description: The fatal Learjet crash is prompting some wealthy public figures to reconsider traveling by private plane.

news.title: Elon Musk deleted his message urging people to vote Republican
news.description: The “vote red” message posted by Elon Musk disappeared after Election Day.

news.title: Google disables Gemini and AI Search by default in schools
news.description: Google has finally made Gemini, Gemini Notebook and Search disabled by default for schools, following controversy over the inability to turn off certain AI features without losing Search. DuckDuckGo published instructions for changing the default search engine and accused Google of imposing AI on children.

news.title: Uber’s AI agents booked only four rides during Halloween
news.description: During Halloween week, AI agents booked just four Uber rides and about 500 food orders, out of roughly 320 million rides and orders. The CEO says adoption remains very limited, partly because booking manually takes about 50 seconds.

news.title: Meta acquires Conductor, a specialist in coordinating coding agents
news.description: Meta acquired Conductor, a startup whose interface directs multiple coding agents simultaneously. Its hosted service will shut down on November 20.

news.title: AI-linked PACs spend millions in the midterm elections
news.description: AI-focused political action committees spent millions during the midterm elections, with mixed results. They spent $4.8 million on a South Carolina Senate candidate who lost, among other campaigns.

news.title: Nothing will launch an AI product with no new screen in December
news.description: Nothing CEO Carl Pei announced that the company’s first product designed natively around AI would launch in December. He said it would not have a new screen.

news.title: Asian AI-related stocks plunge
news.description: Asian AI-related stocks fell, with SoftBank down 5.3%, Tokyo Electron down 7.7% and Advantest down 9.4%.

news.title: Moonshot releases the open weights of its Kimi K3.1 Pro model
news.description: Moonshot released Kimi K3.1 Pro with open, downloadable weights, text and image understanding, and a one-million-token memory. The model is distributed under a custom license and can be tried on HuggingChat.

news.title: Apple opens the Apple Intelligence developer beta in China
news.description: Apple opened an Apple Intelligence developer beta in China featuring Writing Tools, Genmoji and a version of Siri assisted by Qwen. A public version is expected in December.

news.title: True leaders need champions and partners
news.description: The editorial argues that true leaders do not need consultants, but champions and partners.

news.title: The Lake Geneva region surpasses Zurich in economic weight
news.description: According to new estimates from the Federal Statistical Office, Switzerland’s economic map has been redrawn, and the Lake Geneva region now surpasses Zurich in economic weight.

news.title: Scientific debate over AI consciousness intensifies
news.description: The possibility that artificial intelligences may one day possess a form of consciousness is becoming the subject of growing scientific debate.

news.title: Ancient retroviruses may have differentiated human and chimpanzee brains
news.description: Retroviral infections that occurred millions of years ago may have contributed to differentiating human and chimpanzee brains.

news.title: A brain–machine interface reveals consciousness in unresponsive patients
news.description: In patients hospitalized in intensive care after an acute brain injury and unable to respond clinically, a brain–machine interface revealed hidden consciousness.

news.title: Japan performs first post-approval iPS cell transplant for Parkinson’s
news.description: Japan has carried out the first post-approval iPS cell transplant as part of a treatment for Parkinson’s disease.

news.title: The LHC collides oxygen to study the early Universe
news.description: CERN’s Large Hadron Collider has carried out oxygen collisions for the first time to probe the earliest moments of the Universe.

news.title: An AI Website Model with Dual Interfaces for Humans and Agents
news.description: A new study conducted with Knotch proposes websites with two surfaces: an intent-responsive interface for humans and a service-oriented semantic interface for agents. Both would rely on a shared brand context model capable of keeping the company’s content, rules, and capabilities up to date.
